The author, a disabled millennial, expresses feeling fortunate just to leave the house, highlighting the growing isolation faced by disabled individuals in Britain. New research from Scope reveals that nearly half of working-age disabled people experience chronic loneliness, equating to about 3 million people. With Britain already dubbed the "loneliness capital of Europe," the study underscores a severe epidemic of isolation among disabled individuals, emphasizing stark social disconnection rather than mere emotional loneliness.
